item.text:
Using the local structured prior as the baseline, and not re-fetching the country-year datasets already supplied, here is the compact 2022 research set for Erdoğan. I am not scoring.

**Office, authority, constraints**
- Erdoğan was the **President of the Republic of Türkiye** in 2022.
- Under the 1982 Constitution as amended in 2017, the president is the **head of state** and holds **executive power**. The president can appoint ministers and senior officials, command the armed forces through the constitutional framework, and issue presidential decrees on executive matters.
- The constraints matter too: presidential decrees cannot regulate fundamental/political rights, cannot cover areas reserved exclusively to statute, and are subject to constitutional review.
- The presidency is a **5-year elected office**, with a **two-term cap**, and the National Assembly can trigger renewed elections by a **3/5 majority**. That makes 2022 a pre-election year inside a strongly presidentialized but still legally bounded system.

**Retained sources**
| Source | Why keep it |
|---|---|
| [Constitution of the Republic of Türkiye](https://anayasa.gov.tr/tr/mevzuat/anayasa/) | **Publisher:** Anayasa Mahkemesi. **Date:** 1982, amended 2017. **Precise fact:** Articles 101, 104, and 116 establish direct election, 5-year terms, the two-term cap, executive power in the presidency, decree limits, and parliamentary renewal power. **Period fit:** This is the governing legal frame for 2022. **Ruler attribution:** Structural authority, not personal conduct. **Limitations:** Legal text only. **Contrary point:** Parliament and courts still exist; presidential power is not unlimited. |
| [Press Release concerning the Decisions on the Presidential Decrees](https://www.anayasa.gov.tr/en/news/constitutionality-review/press-release-concerning-the-decisions-on-the-presidential-decrees/) | **Publisher:** Constitutional Court of Türkiye. **Date:** 2020-05-15. **Precise fact:** Presidential decrees are reviewable and bounded by subject-matter limits; they cannot displace law on protected categories. **Period fit:** Explains the operating constraints in 2022. **Ruler attribution:** Shows what Erdoğan could do institutionally, not what he chose to do. **Limitations:** Judicial interpretation, not event reporting. **Contrary point:** Still confirms broad executive decree power inside the executive sphere. |
| [Akkuyu NGS'nin dördüncü reaktörünün temeli atıldı](https://enerji.gov.tr/haber-detay?id=21000) | **Publisher:** T.C. Enerji ve Tabii Kaynaklar Bakanlığı. **Date:** 2022-07-21. **Precise fact:** Official ministry announcement marks the start of Akkuyu Unit 4 construction and frames it as a major national energy project. **Period fit:** Direct 2022 nuclear-policy context. **Ruler attribution:** Officially tied to Erdoğan-era energy strategy, but not a personal decision log. **Limitations:** Government framing, not independent assessment. **Contrary point:** It is about civil nuclear buildout, not nuclear weapons or proliferation behavior. |
| [IMF Staff Completes 2022 Article IV Mission to Türkiye](https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2022/11/04/pr22372-turkiye-imf-staff-completes-2022-article-iv-mission-to-turkiye) | **Publisher:** IMF. **Date:** 2022-11-04. **Precise fact:** IMF says late-2021 rate cuts increased vulnerabilities, were followed by lira depreciation and high inflation, and war-in-Ukraine shocks worsened the external position. **Period fit:** Direct read on the 2022 macro environment. **Ruler attribution:** Strong for policy context and inherited conditions; not a personal-performance score. **Limitations:** Staff mission statement, not Board-endorsed final report. **Contrary point:** Also credits the rebound to private-sector dynamics and stimulative policy, so the picture is mixed. |
| [Press Release on Interest Rates (2022-42)](https://tcmb.gov.tr/wps/wcm/connect/en/tcmb%2Ben/main%2Bmenu/announcements/press%2Breleases/2022/ano2022-42) | **Publisher:** Central Bank of the Republic of Türkiye. **Date:** 2022-10-20. **Precise fact:** The MPC cut the policy rate from 12% to 10.5% while acknowledging inflation and external risks. **Period fit:** Core 2022 economic-policy evidence. **Ruler attribution:** Necessary for the policy backdrop around Erdoğan, even though the text is institutional. **Limitations:** Official central-bank language softens political pressure. **Contrary point:** The bank still states price stability as its primary objective. |
| [Turkish central bank to cut rates to 11% after Erdogan nudge](https://www.investing.com/news/economy/turkish-central-bank-to-cut-rates-to-11-after-erdogan-nudge-2916678) | **Publisher:** Reuters, syndicated by Investing.com. **Date:** 2022-10-20. **Precise fact:** Reuters reports markets expected another cut after Erdoğan publicly pushed for lower rates despite high inflation. **Period fit:** Sharp ruler-specific attribution for the 2022 macro story. **Ruler attribution:** High. It links Erdoğan’s public stance to the rate-cut cycle. **Limitations:** Secondary reporting and market expectation, not a formal policy record. **Contrary point:** It does not by itself prove a direct order to the central bank. |
| [Russia, Ukraine seal landmark grains-export deal in Istanbul](https://www.euronews.com/2022/07/23/uk-ukraine-crisis-grain-turkey-deal-int) | **Publisher:** Reuters via Euronews. **Date:** 2022-07-23. **Precise fact:** Türkiye was one of the brokers/signatories to the Black Sea grain deal in Istanbul. **Period fit:** One of the biggest foreign-policy events of 2022. **Ruler attribution:** Strong for Erdoğan’s diplomacy and mediation role. **Limitations:** Diplomatic success story; not a neutral audit of bargaining power. **Contrary point:** The deal was UN-brokered and multilateral, so it is not solely Erdoğan’s achievement. |
| [Cumhurbaşkanı Erdoğan: 'Tahıl koridoru' planının icra ve denetimi İstanbul'da kurulacak merkezden gerçekleşecek](https://www.aa.com.tr/tr/gundem/cumhurbaskani-erdogan-tahil-koridoru-planinin-icra-ve-denetimi-istanbulda-kurulacak-merkezden-gerceklesecek/2643492) | **Publisher:** Anadolu Agency. **Date:** 2022-07-22. **Precise fact:** Erdoğan is quoted as emphasizing implementation/monitoring from Istanbul’s coordination center. **Period fit:** Same grain-corridor event, but in Turkish and closer to the domestic framing. **Ruler attribution:** High, because it is his own public posture. **Limitations:** Favorable government framing. **Contrary point:** It does not independently verify outcomes. |
| [Türkiye to launch Syria ground operation against terrorists 'when convenient': President](https://aa.com.tr/en/turkiye/turkiye-to-launch-syria-ground-operation-against-terrorists-when-convenient-president/2746092) | **Publisher:** Anadolu Agency. **Date:** 2022-11-23. **Precise fact:** Erdoğan signaled a possible ground operation after the November 2022 air campaign. **Period fit:** Central to the security/conflict story in late 2022. **Ruler attribution:** High. **Limitations:** Official narrative, and it does not establish legality or civilian impact. **Contrary point:** The same operation triggered criticism and civilian-harm concerns from rights groups and media. |
| [World Report 2023: Turkey](https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2023/country-chapters/turkey) | **Publisher:** Human Rights Watch. **Date:** World Report 2023. **Precise fact:** HRW says Erdoğan’s government targeted critics, tightened media and judicial control, and escalated the anti-disinformation law ahead of 2023 elections. **Period fit:** Direct synthesis of 2022 conditions. **Ruler attribution:** High for repression, opposition pressure, and institutional capture. **Limitations:** Advocacy report; emphasizes rights harms. **Contrary point:** It still acknowledges some institutional and legal channels remained active. |
| [Türkiye's new 'disinformation law' explained](https://bianet.org/haber/turkiye-s-new-disinformation-law-explained-268523) | **Publisher:** bianet. **Date:** 2022-10-14. **Precise fact:** The new law criminalized “disinformation” with prison terms and expanded state control over online news and press cards. **Period fit:** Directly tied to the 2022 legislative turn before the 2023 election cycle. **Ruler attribution:** High for media-control strategy. **Limitations:** Strongly critical, rights-focused journalism. **Contrary point:** The government presented it as an anti-disinformation measure, not censorship. |
| [Türkiye: ten years of state hostility towards the press under President Erdogan](https://rsf.org/en/t%C3%BCrkiye-ten-years-state-hostility-towards-press-under-president-erdogan) | **Publisher:** Reporters Without Borders. **Date:** 2024-08-10. **Precise fact:** RSF summarizes the long-run press crackdown, including detention, “insulting the president” cases, and platform blocking. **Period fit:** Useful retrospective frame for understanding 2022’s media environment. **Ruler attribution:** High, but broader than 2022 alone. **Limitations:** Advocacy ranking/report, not a case file. **Contrary point:** It is a decade-scale synthesis, so it should not be read as a year-specific event log. |

**Event map**
- January to October 2022: macro stress dominated by rate cuts, lira weakness, and inflation pressure.
- July 22, 2022: Türkiye helped broker/sign the Black Sea grain deal in Istanbul.
- July 21, 2022: Akkuyu Unit 4 construction started, reinforcing the civil nuclear track.
- October 14, 2022: parliament passed the disinformation law.
- October 20, 2022: CBRT cut rates again despite inflation.
- November 2022: Istanbul bombing, then Operation Claw-Sword and Erdoğan’s warning that ground operations could follow.
- All year: opposition/media pressure, judicial control, and conflict spillovers from Syria/Iraq remained part of the ruling environment.

**Chapter source plan**
- 1B: keep the Akkuyu ministry source only if the chapter needs civil nuclear context; otherwise this chapter stays sparse.
- 2B: use IMF, Reuters grain-deal coverage, and Anadolu’s Turkish grain-corridor story, plus the Claw-Sword piece for conflict attribution.
- 3B: use HRW, bianet, and RSF for repression, detainees, and media control.
- 4B: use the Constitution plus HRW/RSF for formal power versus practical democratic constraints.
- 5B: use IMF, CBRT, and Reuters on rate cuts/inflation for the 2022 macro narrative.
- 6B: mostly rely on the supplied local priors; IMF is the best narrative supplement if needed.
- 7B: use HRW, bianet, and RSF for corruption-adjacent institutional abuse, media capture, and anti-accountability pressure.
- 8B: use the Constitution, IMF, and HRW for governance capacity, executive centralization, and inherited institutional weakness.
